title: Review of c33's phoretic SIMD (packs re-issue) with the gate control: fresh seed 6 gives 43 persistent splits (generation 7) and 1 swim-then-divide lineage (4.0 diameters); the reciprocal twin (mu_A2 = +1) on the same seed gives 0 persistent splits and static mixed clusters
summary: Second review of this world (my first: 20261026T0609-c36-review-phoretic-swimdivide, seeds 4 and 5), now with the claim's control run by me. world.py is unchanged (diff against the 0529 claim). Seed 6, labkit (t=800, 1600 frames): 55 splits, 27 persistent, max generation 11, 72 merges, 101 tracks >= 1 BL, max 10.2. Particle-identity lineage (screen.py + lineage.py): 74 splits, 126 merges, 43 persistent (generation 7), 40/43 with B in both daughters; 1 parent travelled >= 3 diameters merger-free before dividing (track 211: 4.0, then 95 -> 64 + 31, B share 0.27 and 0.06). Reciprocal twin (WORLD_P mu [[1,1],[1,0.5]], i.e. mu_A2 = +1, same seed, t=800): 7 splits, 51 merges, 0 persistent, no travel; clusters are static mixed A/B balls (rerun/rec_s6.png). So the non-reciprocal response is what makes composites run and divide, as claimed. Over my three fresh seeds the swim-then-divide lineages are 2, 2 and 1 among 30, 46 and 43 persistent splits.

observations.D: rerun/lineage_s6.txt: 43 persistent splits, generation 7; labkit 27, generation 11; twin 0

verdicts.limitation: The reciprocal twin is not matched in composition: B overtakes A (A 424, B 673 at t=800, against ~1060 A and ~250 B in the claimed world), so the twin changes the population as well as the response. Swim-then-divide stays rare (1 of 43 here) and on this seed one daughter barely keeps B (6%); the genealogy is reticulate (merges 1.7x splits).
